assignments.note: 2023-07 Can LLMs write good property-based tests
assignments.why: LLM-generated property-based test sets (self-evolving tests) used as execution-based verification of code (alternative evaluation paradigms).
Measures style-over-factuality bias of LLM and human raters (audits) and proposes Multi-Elo rating to make judges less biased (LLM and agent judges).
Self-hosted web environments with 812 agent tasks graded by functional state checks, with documented verifier failures.
Eight interactive environments for scoring LLMs as agents.
Multi-persona LLM judge design (judges), evaluation by multi-agent debate (alternative paradigms), and a final verdict aggregated across several judges (social choice).
A fine-tuned 7B critic trained on community critiques (trained judges) whose subject is critiquing model answers (LLM judges).
Benchmark measuring six cognitive biases across 15 LLM judges (audits), with order bias among the central measured effects (presentation sensitivity).
Method that raises LLM-judge agreement with experts (judges) by drafting and refining its own scoring criteria from where it misses human labels (self-improving judge).
Generates reasoning test samples on the fly from DAGs with controllable complexity.
Multi-turn tool-use evaluation harness (benchmarks) with GPT-4-simulated natural-language user feedback (user simulation).
A method to make LLM judges more consistent (judges) by removing position bias through split-and-merge alignment (presentation sensitivity).
LM-emulated sandbox for agent risk evaluation (benchmarks), an LM safety evaluator scoring trajectories (agent judges), and an adversarial emulator steering into risky states (adversarial tests).

assignments.note: 2023-10 A Long Way to Go Length Correlations in RLHF
assignments.why: Empirical study (audits) showing RLHF reward models (trained RMs, preference learning) learn response length as a shortcut.
A 13B fine-tuned generative judge (trained judges) doing pairwise and critique-with-rating evaluation (LLM judges).
Accepts code only when code, docstring and Dafny annotations are mutually consistent under a verifier: consistency checks and execution/formal verification.

assignments.note: 2023-10 Evaluating large language models at evaluating instruction following LLMBar
assignments.why: LLMBar is a meta-evaluation benchmark of judges on adversarial pairs (audits) and tests prompting strategies such as Rules, Swap and Metrics+Reference to improve judges (LLM judges).
Fine-tuned pairwise judges (trained judges, LLM judges) with swap augmentation specifically to remove position bias (presentation sensitivity).

assignments.note: 2023-10 Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
assignments.why: Empirical measurement (audits) showing an LLM judging and correcting its own reasoning without external feedback fails (the act of self-judging).
Attacker LLM iteratively refines adversarial jailbreak prompts from the target's replies and judge scores.
A fine-tuned 13B rubric-conditioned judge (trained judges) as an open substitute for GPT-4 grading (LLM judges).

assignments.note: 2023-10 Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
assignments.why: Worst-case and uncertainty-weighted reward-model ensembles (trained RMs) against overoptimization in RLHF-style BoN and PPO (preference learning).
Role-play environment for evaluating social agents (benchmarks) scored on seven dimensions by a GPT-4 judge, SOTOPIA-EVAL (LLM judges).
Agent benchmark of real GitHub issues with documented verifier failures (benchmarks), graded by running the repo's unit tests on the patch (execution-based verification).
A trained reward model (trained judges) that calls calculators, code interpreters and search before scoring (agentic judge that runs code).
Measures GPT-4's verbosity bias relative to humans and proposes a metric for it.
Compares debate against consultancy as a way for judges to reach correct answers.
466 tool- and browsing-heavy assistant tasks graded by quasi-exact final-answer match.
An adversarial attacker LLM generates new red-team prompts against the current target in alternating rounds.

assignments.note: 2023-11 Scalable AI safety via doubly-efficient debate
assignments.why: Theoretical debate protocols where the honest debater wins and the judge checks only a constant number of steps.
Benchmarks multi-agent debate strategies (debate) against self-consistency and ensembling, i.e. vote aggregation over several agents' outputs (social choice).
